name: Gloucester Avenue (Hip Strip)
description: A one kilometre seafront run of bars, jerk shacks, craft stalls, dive shops and small hotels, with Doctor's Cave Beach halfway along. It is patrolled, busy and the only genuinely walkable part of Montego Bay. Most short-stay visitors and anyone without a car bases here.
bestFor: Nomads on a short stay who want to live without renting a car.
pros: Walk to beaches, bars and restaurants
Visible police and tourist police presence
cons: Bar noise runs late along the strip

name: Ironshore
tagline: Condos and villas on the coast road
description: A residential belt roughly seven kilometres east of the Hip Strip, made up of gated villa streets, condo complexes, a golf course and the Whitter Village shopping centre. It is where most longer-term foreign residents live, quiet at night and stocked with real supermarkets rather than resort shops.
bestFor: Nomads staying a month or more who want a normal apartment and a supermarket run.
pros: Best value for a proper apartment or villa
Supermarkets and pharmacies, not just tourist shops
Quiet, gated and calm after dark
cons: You really need a car or steady taxi budget
Little walkable nightlife or cafe life
Coast road traffic slows badly at rush hour

name: Rose Hall
tagline: Gated resort belt east of town
description: The all-inclusive corridor about twelve kilometres east, running from the Rose Hall Great House past Half Moon and the big beachfront resorts, with championship golf inland. Private beaches, manicured grounds and total security, but almost nothing outside the gates. A base for comfort rather than local life.
bestFor: Nomads with the budget for a resort condo who value calm and security above all.
pros: Private beaches and reliable resort infrastructure
Golf, spas and good restaurants on site
cons: Completely cut off from local life
Every trip out means a taxi of $20 or more each way

name: Freeport
description: A flat reclaimed peninsula southwest of downtown holding the cruise pier, the Montego Bay Yacht Club and low-rise condo complexes on wide, near-empty roads. It is calm, breezy and secure, popular with residents who want a marina view. Nothing much happens here beyond cruise ship days.
bestFor: Nomads who want a quiet, breezy condo and do not mind driving into town.
pros: Very quiet with sea breeze on three sides
Condos with pools at fair prices
Secure and easy to walk or run around
cons: Almost no restaurants or shops nearby
Cruise ship days flood the roads
Car or taxi needed for everything

name: Downtown Montego Bay
description: The commercial heart around Sam Sharpe Square, the craft market and Charles Gordon Market, packed with route taxis, street vendors, banks and hardware shops. It is by far the cheapest place to rent and eat, and it is where the city actually functions, but it is not set up for visitors.
bestFor: Budget nomads with Caribbean experience who want local prices, not a resort bubble.
pros: Cheapest rents and meals in the city
Route taxis reach everywhere for under $2
cons: Not a sensible base after dark, avoid walking at night
Higher street crime than the tourist corridor
Noisy, congested and short on decent rentals
